title: Classify the seven requests
prompt: Place each request in the approach that fits it.
categories: Live action or MCP, not indexing

pairs.item: Policy wiki: in-house, 38,400 pages, REST API with per-page read groups; staff want cited answers.
pairs.why: No native connector, document-like content, and permissions available through the API.

pairs.item: Vendor learning system: no native connector, 12,000 courses, enrollment-based visibility, offset pagination.
pairs.why: Document-like content with no native option. Flag offset pagination: it is unstable while the source is being written to.

pairs.item: Reference archive: no API, but a nightly HTML export with a file listing read groups.
pairs.why: Scoping covers the no-API case: can the source export content to external storage?

pairs.item: Drive team wants a Clinic ID filter on files the native Drive connector already indexes.
pairs.why: Use the existing connector first. Custom Metadata attaches to native documents without re-indexing.

pairs.item: Claims warehouse: 410 million rows; analysts ask for denial rates by payer.
pairs.category: Live action or MCP, not indexing
pairs.why: For large structured data lakes, query with a custom action or MCP server.

pairs.item: Facility telemetry: freezer temperatures every 10 seconds.
pairs.category: Live action or MCP, not indexing
pairs.why: Glean is not a data analytics platform for time series or sensor data.

pairs.item: Bed board: availability changes every few minutes; nurses place holds.
pairs.category: Live action or MCP, not indexing
pairs.why: Freshness dominates and an action is required.

takeaway: Three of seven need a custom connector. The other four are better served another way.
